name: MonarchCalendarHeatmap
title: CalendarHeatmap
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout (Row, Column, BoxWithConstraints) with Modifier.drawBehind and Modifier.horizontalScroll, inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchHeatmap's scale and legend
summary: Values by day on a calendar grid, a contribution-style year or a month calendar with day numbers, binned into four color steps with a Less to More legend, today, notes, non-working days, markers, tap inspection, drill-in and the days as a table.
whenToUse: To show a daily measure over weeks or months where the weekday and the season matter, such as commits, hours worked or check-ins.
whenNotToUse: For a matrix whose rows and columns are not days use MonarchHeatmap. For a trend over time use MonarchLineChart or MonarchSparkline. To pick a date use the Material 3 DatePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCalendarHeatmap(title: String, days: List<MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, from: Long? = null, to: Long? = null, description: String? = null, layout: MonarchCalendarHeatmapLayout = MonarchCalendarHeatmapLayout.Year, today: Long? = null, firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, color: MonarchChartColor = MonarchChartColor.Data1, thresholds: List<Double>? = null, showValues: Boolean = true, showLegend: Boolean = true, summary: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, labels: MonarchCalendarHeatmapLabels = MonarchCalendarHeatmapLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(date: Long, value: Double?, valueLabel: String? = null, note: String? = null, inactive: Boolean = false, marker: Boolean = false)

class MonarchCalendarHeatmapLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), less: String? = null, more: String? = null, noData: String? = null, rangeBelow: String? = null, above: String? = null, range: String? = null, rangeAbove: String? = null, date: String? = null, value: String? = null, note: String? = null, today: String? = null, inactive: String? = null, marker: String? = null, dayCount: ((days: Int) -> String)? = null, summary: String? = null, highest: String? = null, select: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading.

options.name: days
options.description: One entry per day with something to show: a date (epoch milliseconds, UTC), a value (null for no data), and optional value text, note, non-working flag and marker. Days in the range without an entry are no data; a later entry for the same day wins.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the frame.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day drawn, as epoch milliseconds in UTC. The earliest entry when null.

options.name: to
options.description: The last day drawn, as epoch milliseconds in UTC. The latest entry when null.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: layout
options.description: Year: weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, scrolling sideways; Month: a calendar with day numbers and values.

options.name: today
options.description: The day ringed as today, as epoch milliseconds in UTC. Passed by the app; the component never reads the clock.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first day of the week as a java.util.Calendar constant (Calendar.MONDAY). null uses the current locale's.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. Ready without an entry in the range shows Empty.

options.name: color
options.description: The data color of the four steps.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when null.

options.name: showValues
options.description: Month layout: writes each day's value text (or note) under its number when the day is at least 44dp wide.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Shows the Less to More legend under the grid.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary TalkBack reads for the grid.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the frame's, the legend's, the table headings, Today, Non-working day, Marked, the day count, the summary, the highest day and the Select action.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values. A number in the current locale by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the day when it is tapped or chosen with the TalkBack Select action; a day without an entry comes with value null.

states.name: level
states.description: Each day with a value takes one of five fills: the muted background for zero, then the data color mixed in at 25%, 50% and 75%, then the data color itself.

states.name: no data
states.description: A day in the range without a value is empty with a hairline in the subtle border color.

states.name: non-working
states.description: A day marked inactive without a value above zero has the subtle background and a dashed outline, and is read "Non-working day".

states.name: today
states.description: The day of today has a thick outline in the accent color and is read "Today".

states.name: inspected
states.description: After a tap the day has a thick outline in the default text color, is selected for TalkBack, and its date, value and notes are written under the grid in a polite live region.

states.name: marker
states.description: A day with marker has a small dot in the warning color in its top end corner and is read "Marked".

states.name: month values
states.description: In the month layout a day at least 44dp wide writes its value text, its value or its note under its number; on the two strongest steps the text sits on a surface chip.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" lists every day with an entry: date, value and, when any day has one, note.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The frame's skeleton, empty state and error with Try again, at the chart's height.

appearance: Steps mix the chosen data color into the muted background, as MonarchHeatmap does; non-working days use the subtle background, outlines the subtle and default border colors, today the accent color, the inspected day the default text color and markers the warning color. Weekday and month names are in the muted text color. Every color is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web draws an SVG that shrinks a year to fit the width; on Android, as on iOS, the year keeps 14dp days and scrolls sideways on a phone, opening at the latest week. Days are epoch milliseconds in UTC compared as whole days (minSdk 24 has no java.time without desugaring), and date, weekday and month names come from android.icu in the current locale; the web takes ISO date strings and weekStartsOn, which is firstDayOfWeek here (iOS uses the environment's Calendar). The inspected day is internal state, not a controlled activeDate. There is no keyboard navigation (arrows, Page Up/Down) and no floating tooltip: the inspected day is written under the grid. Android has no chart descriptor like iOS's AXChartDescriptor (Audio Graphs) and no adjustable element: in both layouts every day is its own TalkBack element, in date order. Non-working days and markers are also read as words ("Non-working day", "Marked"), which the web leaves to the note.
accessibility: The grid is a traversal group whose content description is the generated summary ("8 days from Thu, Jan 1, 2026 to Thu, Jan 8, 2026. Total 28. Highest: Tue, Jan 6, 2026: 12 commits") or summary.

Every day in the range is one TalkBack element in date order, read as its date and its value or No data, followed by its note, Non-working day, Marked and Today as they apply; weekday and month names are hidden.
The inspected day carries the selected state.
With onSelect each day has a TalkBack custom action "Select"; days have no click action, because year days are 14dp, far below the 48dp target, and a tap on them is a convenience.
The inspection line under the grid is a polite live region, so a newly inspected day is announced.
The legend is one element read as its name and the range of every step.
Zero, no data, non-working days, today and markers differ by fill, outline and dot, and are also in the spoken text and the table, not color alone.
Weeks are laid out from the start edge, so they mirror right to left.
edgeCases: A range that ends before it starts, no entries and no range, or no entry inside the range shows the empty state.
Any time of a UTC day counts as that day; the device's time zone does not shift days.
In the year layout days are 14dp; the tap is a convenience and TalkBack uses the Select action.
At the largest font size weekday names may overlap the empty rows between them, month names are skipped when they would overlap, and month days grow taller.
Tap inspection, the horizontal scroll and TalkBack were checked with Robolectric tests, not on a device with TalkBack; the dates, model, styles, text and summary are unit-tested.

examples.title: A month of hours with holidays and drill-in
examples.code:
MonarchCalendarHeatmap(
    title = "Hours",
    days = listOf(
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(january, null, note = "Holiday", inactive = true),
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(january + day, 7.5, valueLabel = "7h 30m"),
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(january + 2 * day, 8.0, marker = true, note = "On call"),
    ),
    from = january,
    to = january + 30 * day,
    layout = MonarchCalendarHeatmapLayout.Month,
    firstDayOfWeek = java.util.Calendar.MONDAY,
    footer = opened,
    onSelect = { opened = it.valueLabel ?: "No hours" },
)
